content:
Mathlib's FunLike interface offers a "universal" extensionality lemma, docs#DFunLike.ext, which is just returning one of the proof fields of the DFunLike typeclass.

I notice this is not tagged with the @[ext] flag which makes it available to the ext tactic; instead there are dozens of special-case lemmas specializing DFunLike.ext to particular types (Finsupp.ext, OuterMeasure.ext, Valuation.ext, ContinuousMonoidHom.ext, etc) which do have the @[ext] tag, and are proved as one-line applications of the general DFunLike.ext lemma.

Is this just an oversight? Or is there a specific reason why the general lemma is not @[ext]?

There was a specific reason, but I'm having trouble remembering what it is, and both my ideas I suspect are no longer relevant. I thought it was either that Lean had trouble applying the general one to explicit morphisms, or that this would somehow interfere with morphism-specific ext lemmas (like the Basis one for linear maps), but I can't envision what the mechanism is that would prevent either of these from working normally.
If you make the general lemma ext and remove the attribute on the others, does anything break?
The issue is that ext keys on the type of the conclusion, but the type of the conclusion of docs#DFinsupp.ext is a free variable
If ext used a DiscrTree then this would still be fine (if perhaps non-performant), but I'm not sure if it did or does.
Oh right, DFunLike.coe doesn't appear in the conclusion, of course. So there's no place to read off the FunLike instance.
Should we mention this in a comment near docs#DFunLike.ext?

Thomas Browning said:

Should we mention this in a comment near docs#DFunLike.ext?

That was my thought as well. I’ll make a PR shortly.
